Jordan / procurement team —

Thanks for the productive call this morning. As discussed, attaching a baseline CAPEX/workload model that maps HelioSystems' projected peak QPS and steady-state TPU/GPU mix into reserved capacity buckets. Also attached is our standard commit term proposal (redwood_commit_terms_v1.pdf) with the two-tier discount table.

Quick summary of ask from our side:
- Confirm desired baseline reserved GPUs (we sketched 50 GPUs baseline on the call).
- Preferred commit tenor: 12 months vs 24 months (we can offer deeper discounts at 24 months).
- Expected quarterly scale window needs (how many GPUs you may want to scale up/down at quarter boundaries).
- Any procurement constraints (purchase order timing, legal redlines).

Notes on GPU pricing sensitivity: the CAPEX sheet includes three scenarios (base, +10% GPU market shock, -10% GPU pricing improvement). These feed into required discount tiers to keep Helio's per-token economics within target. If you expect more aggressive GPU volatility we recommend a 24-month with a pass-through clause capped at +/- 15% to avoid us needing a >20% discount.

Next steps: can you confirm the baseline and preferred term by EOD Friday? I can run finance scenarios and flag any discount approvals needed before we produce a term sheet.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Connor —

Thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers from our side before we loop in procurement/legal:
- Baseline reserve: we are comfortable starting at 50 A100-equivalent GPUs, with the ability to spike to 80 for product launches.
- Term: leaning toward 24 months for stability, but we need a quarterly adjustment window (we can exercise +/- 10 GPUs at quarter boundary).
- Volatility: our finance team is worried about GPU-market swings; a pass-through is acceptable but they asked whether Redwood can absorb short-term shocks within a 10% band. Anything beyond that they want price-protection triggers.

Looping in Alan Singh (finance) and procurement@ for PO process and legal redlines. Also cc'd finance@heliosystems.com for visibility.

—Jordan

Folks —

Looping in Karthik for engineering sizing confirmation and finance for discount thresholds. My take: Helio is a strategic mid-market account with potential to expand into dedicated fleets across two regions next year. We can be more aggressive on price if: 1) they sign 24 months, 2) baseline >= 50 GPUs, and 3) they commit to quarterly scale windows rather than ad-hoc spikes.

Attached is an internal pricing sensitivity slide with three approval bands:
- Manager sign-off allowed up to 10% effective discount vs list.
- Director approval required for 10–20% effective discount.
- VP/CFO approval required for anything >20% (rare).

If Helio insists on Redwood absorbing >10% GPU-market shock, we should ask for a contingency clause (cap on absolute pass-through) or a higher baseline with staged ramp to reduce unit exposure. Connor, can you make the ask explicit to procurement: (A) prefer 24-month; (B) baseline 50; (C) quarterly scale windows of +/-10 GPUs; (D) cap pass-through at +/-15% with a review clause at 12 months.

-Marissa

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the quick reply and for looping procurement/finance. Per internal guidance below, here are two concrete paths for your review (I laid numbers into the CAPEX sheet and attached a one‑page summary):

Option A — 12 months (flex window monthly):
- Baseline: 50 GPUs
- Discount: 12% off list
- Scale: monthly +/- 5 GPUs (with 7-day notice)
- GPU shock: pass-through applies at >10% market movement

Option B — 24 months (preferred for pricing stability):
- Baseline: 50 GPUs
- Discount: 18% off list; 22% off list if baseline >= 75 GPUs
- Scale: quarterly window +/- 10 GPUs
- GPU shock: pass-through applies outside +/-15% cap; any request to absorb >15% requires VP approval

If you confirm Option B (24 months, baseline 50, quarterly +/-10), we will prepare a term sheet and route for director-level approval (Karthik to confirm engineering sizing and Neha to confirm finance assumptions). If Helio wants us to absorb shocks within +/-10% without pass-through, we will need a higher baseline or a blended price that effectively reduces unit discount.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- Term: 24 months with quarterly scale windows of +/-10 GPUs
- Baseline reserve: 50 A100-eq GPUs; ability to spike to 80 for launches (we will provide quarterly forecasts)
- Pricing: accept the 18% discount. We request Redwood cap the pass-through at +/-15% (as outlined) and include a 12-month review clause to re-open terms if the GPU cost index moves >20%.
- Next step: please send a term sheet and an initial PO template. Procurement/legal will need the standard SOW and a redline-friendly PDF.

Also for internal planning, can Redwood provide a brief run-rate projection for our CFO that shows expected monthly spend under three GPU-market scenarios (base / +10% / -10%)? If you can attach that to the term sheet that would speed approval.
